newsitem.title: USA: Octel says to delay product release.
newsitem.headline: Octel says to delay product release.

text.p: Octel Communications Corp will delay the release of a new version of its voice processing computers by up to six months, said Greg Klaben, the company's director of investor relations.

Octel, which makes computers that store voice mail on telephone networks, said in a conference call with financial analysts earlier that the delay of its Sierra product was caused by a software glitch.
Some analysts, including Merrill Lynch's Joseph Bellace, cut earnings forecasts due to the delay.
"We prefer to ship a fully functional product without bugs than one which might need to be repaired," Klaben said.

Sierra was expected to be shipped in the company's fiscal second quarter ending in December. Klaben said it will now "probably" ship in the company's third fiscal quarter, but "possibly" would not ship until the fourth quarter.
In early afternoon trading, Octel shares were down 8-5/8 at 15-7/8 on Nasdaq trading of 16.4 million shares, making the issue the most active on the market.

Klaben declined to comment about the impact of the delay on Octel's earnings in the coming quarter, but he said the consensus of analyst forecasts for the fiscal year ending June 1997 slipped to $1.10 a share from $1.25 following the news.
